From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: ACME kickoff recap & proposed next steps (streaming / tool-calls)

Hi Claire / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary evaluation goals: validate streaming latency under your expected request patterns, confirm tool-calling + structured outputs for order-extraction pipeline, and compare output determinism vs your current hyperscaler integration.
- Success criteria we heard: streaming tail latency < 250ms per chunk for 99th, structured JSON accuracy > 95% on the extraction test set, and no regression in cost-per-1000-tokens beyond 15% of your current baseline.

Proposed immediate tests (we can execute these together):
1) Streaming test: run live 1000-request batch using your sample traffic (we'll instrument latency at chunk-level).
2) Tool-calling end-to-end: validate calls to your internal order-service stub with function schemas and confirm schema adherence and retry behavior.
3) Structured outputs: run the 500-record extraction set you shared and compute precision/recall.

Attachments: I attached a high-level matrix where we mapped Redwood vs a representative hyperscaler on feature parity + our recommended test harness (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.xlsx). Also dropping a stub MAP (acme-mutual-action-plan.docx) for timeline.

Next logistics: can we schedule the execution window for the streaming test this Tue 8/3 between 10-12 PT? If that works, we will provision a dedicated test queue and invite your infra lead so we can tweak load shapes.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short Doc with test runner commands and expected outputs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0198

---
Note: We will only use sanitized sample data; full privacy/security checklist will be shared if you want to run on prod traffic.

Hi Claire / Samir — looping in a couple technical details and what we'll need from your side for the runs.

Streaming test plan (high-level):
- We'll run a continuous-stream workload of 1k requests using your sample traces. Each request will be measured for per-chunk latency and end-to-end throughput.
- We will expose metrics via a temporary Prom endpoint and push to your Grafana if you'd like.
- Required from Acme: a short token for the staging order-service (or a stub we can hit) and the traffic trace file.

Tool-calling behavior notes:
- Redwood supports function/tool calling with strict schema validation + optional automatic retry. Default behavior is at-least-once for transient errors; we can toggle to at-most-once in the client config.
- We'll instrument call ids so you can correlate downstream events.

Hyperscaler baseline: we can run the HCloud v2 baseline side-by-side. To make it fair we'll align sequence lengths, sampling/temp settings, and batching window. If you can share existing invocation code or an example request, we will replicate it.

Costs: for the initial 2-hour streaming run + tooling work and the 500-record structured test, estimate is ~$1,200 in run costs + a 2-day engineering time estimate for setup/analysis. Marissa — can you confirm if we want Redwood to issue an official test quote or if the customer would prefer a T&E credit?

A few technical caveats to call out up front:
- Streaming chunk size and model context length will affect chunk latency - we'll run a short calibration first.
- If you plan to evaluate quantized variants, we should do a quality regression check on your extraction set before swapping defaults.

Happy to run the schedule during Tue 10-12PT. Samir — do you want a quick 15-min sync Mon 8/2 to hand off artifacts?

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery@redwood.ai
